## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

It sets out proper etiquette regarding the consumption of meals, specifically proscribing the breaking up of mouthfuls of food. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In other Vinaya traditions, full parallels are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages.
